newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. mull $1 million-a-year panda lease.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. mull $1 million-a-year panda lease.

text.p: China is considering leasing two giant pandas to a U.S. zoo for around $1 million a year but talks on the deal have been stalled for two months, the China Daily said on Saturday.

The panda lease was seen as a goodwill gesture by China ahead of a planned visit to the United States by Chinese President Jiang Zemin, but terms had yet to be agreed, the newspaper quoted Ministry of Construction officials as saying.
Jiang is expected to make a state visit to Washington later this year.
China was asking the Atlanta Zoo for an annual donation of around $1 million towards wild panda protection and a pledge that the animals would not be used for commercial purposes, the newspaper said.

Chinese negotiators required approval from the State Council, or cabinet, while the Atlanta Zoo needed U.S. government certification, the newspaper said, but gave no details of why the talks had stalled.
